design: The deployed v3 builds a weighted opponent range from the complete public action history, with preflop rank/pair/suited merit, historical made-hand percentiles, draw bonuses, and distinct limp/check/call/raise likelihoods. It uses range-weighted showdown equity to price calls and combines value betting with moderate opening and bluff frequencies. It was selected for the highest held-out weighted score among the three finalists; the later pressure and raise-size variants did not demonstrate a convincing improvement.

verdicts.v1: Kept as parent of v2. The executable baseline scored +17.80, but lost substantially to several stronger opponents and the aggressor probe.
verdicts.v2: Kept as the modeling foundation for v3 and v4. Its +17.12 score did not improve on v1 within sampling uncertainty; the draw and limp changes were retained for their explicit poker interpretation, not claimed as a measured gain.
verdicts.v3: Kept as parent of v5 and selected for deployment. Development +23.12 and held-out +25.07 were consistent; +25.07 was the highest finalist held-out score. Its slightly negative parent matches are an explicit warning, not evidence of a clear loss or win.
verdicts.v4: Discarded. Discounting all range evidence reduced the weighted score to +0.78 and caused large losses against much of the stronger field.
verdicts.v5: Discarded as a deployment candidate. Development +23.15 was only 0.03 above v3; held-out +24.17 was below v3. Parent results +2.49 (SE 7.85, seed 2) and +9.37 (SE 11.53, seed 1000) were inconclusive. The extra bluffing and wider openings were not established improvements.
verdicts.v6: Uniform-hand control of v5 only; not eligible for deployment. Its -120.75 field score, compared with v5 +23.15 at the same seed and sample size, demonstrated the value of action-based range conditioning for that policy.
verdicts.v7: Discarded. The raise-size model changed the intended diagnostic range but did not improve the primary score: +22.90 development and +24.56 held out. It adds 11 decision lines, and its parent result -5.56 (SE 7.20) was inconclusive. It supplied no compelling reason to replace v3.
verdicts.v8: Uniform-hand control of v3 only; not eligible for deployment. Its -76.91 field score and large direct loss to v3 support retaining the range model.

ablation: The deployed v3 uses the same policy and sampling settings as v8, except that v8 sets range_power=0.0, giving every sampled legal holding weight 1. On development seed 0, v3 scored **+23.12** with 32 × 250 hands per opponent; v8 scored **−76.91** with 16 × 250, a **100.03-point** weighted-score difference. The sample sizes differ, so this is not a paired equal-size estimate. In the direct held-out match, v3 beat v8 by **+140.97 bb/100, SE 16.64**, at 32 × 250 hands, seed 1000. Together these support range conditioning for this policy on the tested opponents; they do not establish that the inferred probabilities are calibrated. As an additional equal-size check, v5 scored +23.15 against its uniform control v6 at −120.75 on the same seed-0 field and 32 × 250 size; v5 beat v6 head to head by +123.13 bb/100, SE 21.59, on seed 1000.
choice:
The deployment export is **from .v3 import Bot as DeployedBot**. Each finalist received one field run on held-out seed 1000 at 32 × 250 hands per opponent. Results were **v3 +25.07**, **v7 +24.56**, and **v5 +24.17**. v3 had the highest held-out weighted score. The margins are small relative to the per-opponent uncertainty; this selection is not a claim that v3 is statistically superior to both alternatives. The later variants offered no convincing benefit, so the moderate-pressure v3 was retained. v5 had the highest development score (+23.15 versus v3 +23.12); that 0.03-point difference is noise and was not used to choose it.

The parent warning remains: v3 scored **−2.74 bb/100, SE 9.90**, against v2 on held-out seed 1000, and **−3.02, SE 8.29**, on development seed 1. Against v1, its held-out result was **+1.61, SE 8.17**. These are close to even, so the field advantage is not a demonstrated advantage over related strategies. In the held-out field, material weaknesses included **aggressor −42.64, SE 6.05**, and **faye_gpt −33.77, SE 7.72**. No claim is made to match the prompt’s strongest-bot calibration or to dominate unseen phase-6 lineages.
